clue.text: It's said to get you cleaner

definitions.text: It's said to get you cleaner

parts.words: It's said to get you cleaner
parts.note: read 'you' as said aloud, so it stands for a female sheep, and the clue describes a farm wash that cleans the flock

explanation.walkthrough: 'It's said' looks like hearsay, but it tells you to hear 'you' as EWE: the thing that gets ewes clean.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmer's disinfectant bath that sheep are plunged through to clear them of parasites cleans the ewes.

clue.text: Blue joke held to be brave

indicators.note: held means kept within, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: the sky is the blue
a pun is a joke

explanation.surface: Telling a risque joke takes courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like smutty, chiming with 'joke', but here it is the colour of the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Spunky is informal for plucky, full of courage.

clue.text: Going part of the way, take us to nearby station

indicators.note: going only part of the way through the words means the answer lies within a stretch of them

explanation.surface: A traveller asks a cab driver to take them part of the way to the nearby station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take US TO Nearby' holds the London terminus, EUSTON.
explanation.definitionFit: Euston is a major railway terminus in London.

clue.text: Dividing line sees creative quarter obscured by cloud

indicators.note: something obscured by a cloud is wrapped within it

parts.note: a pall is a cloud, as of smoke
arty means creative
W, west, is a quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: A city's artistic district lies under a cloud of smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creative quarter' reads as an arts district, but it is two pieces: creative, then a compass quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: A shared wall between two houses divides them, marking the line between properties.

parts.note: a clue made of nothing but a question mark has no words at all, so the solver's honest response is the reply

explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the clue is missing: a lone question mark gives you nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase confesses total ignorance, which is the natural reply when given only a question mark.

clue.text: Stupid amount for Chinese dish

parts.note: dim means stupid
a sum is an amount

explanation.surface: Someone is charged a ridiculous price for a Chinese meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Small dumplings and snacks served together form a classic Cantonese dish.

clue.text: Murdoch to her last, as she was born?

parts.note: Iris Murdoch was a novelist

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the word her, tacked on after the name

explanation.surface: Iris Murdoch to the end remained true to her birth.
explanation.walkthrough: Iris Murdoch, the novelist, was born in Dublin, which is what the question mark points to.
explanation.definitionFit: A person born in Dublin is Irish by birth, as the novelist was.

clue.text: Went into power sport

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside another

parts.note: sway is power or influence
went in the sense of relieved oneself, peed

explanation.surface: Someone went into a power sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went' here is the coarse sense, PEED, which goes into SWAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedway is motorcycle racing on an oval dirt track, a spectator sport.

clue.text: Unfortunately, I am short of bread, demanding saucer of milk?

indicators.note: unfortunately implies things going wrong, so the letters after it are shuffled

parts.note: bread is slang for money, so short of it is owing

explanation.surface: Someone poor and short of money pleads for a saucer of milk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunately' rearranges I AM into MIA, then OWING, since bread is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat crying for its saucer of milk mews; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: Spin puts paper against the general flow

indicators.note: to spin something is to turn it about, so the word beside it gets its letters rearranged

parts.note: a ream is a quantity of paper

explanation.surface: A spin doctor puts out a newspaper story contrary to popular opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin' turns PUTS into UPST, followed by REAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Going upstream means moving against the current, a figure for contrary to the general trend.

clue.text: The pictures came in reels

indicators.note: to reel is to stagger dizzily, so the words before it are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A film arrived on its spools, ready to be shown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reels' looks like film spools, but it is the verb, rearranging CAME IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to 'the pictures' is the British idiom for going to see a film at a picture house.

clue.text: Prepare to be catty, say, as means of escape

indicators.note: say means the phrase is spoken, so its sound gives a differently written word

parts.note: a cat about to scratch will get out its claws

explanation.surface: Someone braces themselves to be spiteful as a way out.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract term letting a party withdraw is an escape route from the deal.

clue.text: OK to work by ignoring the odds, which is odd!

indicators.note: skipping the odd-numbered letters keeps only the second, fourth and so on of the words in front

explanation.surface: Someone thinks it is fine to work by defying the odds, and finds that strange.
explanation.walkthrough: Of OKTOWORKBY keep the even letters: K, O, O, K, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Kooky is informal for eccentric or strange, so it means odd.

clue.text: Lid covering end of pipe certainly had now to avoid opening

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: yes is an emphatic certainly

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word now is dropped, so the run loses that one letter

explanation.surface: Someone smoking a pipe has to stop opening their eyelid.
explanation.walkthrough: E from pipe, YES, then HAD NOW without N, the opening of 'now', giving HADOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye make-up is applied as a coloured covering on the eyelid.

clue.text: Pretentiousness evident after Conservative given order: no reason to grumble

indicators.note: after says the next word follows the Conservative-with-order piece

parts.note: cant is insincere, pious or pretentious talk
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
plain means evident

explanation.surface: A Tory gets an honour and their pomposity shows, but nobody has grounds to object.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is a British honour; 'given' simply joins the Conservative to it, and 'after' places 'evident' last.
explanation.definitionFit: The everyday phrase is a reply saying things are fine, so there is nothing to moan about.

clue.text: Convert polyester shifts

indicators.note: shifts means moves around, so the word before is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone converts to polyester dresses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifts' looks like dresses but rearranges POLYESTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A proselyte is a person converted to a new faith, so a convert.

clue.text: Sit within dig, as suggested

indicators.note: within says one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a dig is a poke, a prod
to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: Someone sits in an archaeological dig as advised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dig' looks like an excavation; it is a jab, PROD, holding POSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Proposed means put forward as a suggestion.

clue.text: Overhead locker where witch secretes 6 letters from the grave

indicators.note: secretes means hides away inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a hag is a witch
the answer to 6 down is a nationality whose abbreviation is IR
RIP, rest in peace, is carved on gravestones

explanation.surface: A witch hides letters from a grave in an overhead locker on a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overhead locker' looks like aircraft luggage storage but is a clip locking hair on the head. The 6 is the answer to 6 down, Irish, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: A hair clip on top of the head holds hair locked in place, so it is a locker overhead.

clue.text: Actual place for further distribution

parts.note: real means actual
a location is a place

explanation.surface: A real place is found for handing out more supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Allocating something again means sharing it out a second time, a fresh distribution.

clue.text: See 21
Soak outside toilet on plane, say, finding way through central London

indicators.note: outside says one piece encloses the rest

parts.note: to ret flax is to soak it

indicators.note: on puts the tree piece next to the toilet

parts.note: the gents is a men's toilet
a plane is an example of a tree

explanation.surface: Someone soaks outside an aircraft toilet while finding their way through central London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' suggests aircraft, but it is the tree. Regent Street is a major shopping street in London's West End.
explanation.definitionFit: Regent Street is a famous road running through the West End of London.

clue.text: Mum, having wiped bottom on toilet paper, troubled as such, always going

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so all the letters before it are stirred into a new order
the bottom letter of the word mum is removed, so it is cut at its end

explanation.surface: A lavatory scene in which Mum wipes with loo paper and is upset about it.
explanation.walkthrough: MU (Mum less its last letter) plus ON and TOILET PAPER, all rearranged by 'troubled'.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine in endless motion would keep running forever, never stopping.

clue.text: Something going on smooth tabletop

parts.note: even means smooth or level
the top of table is its first letter, T

explanation.surface: Something is happening on a smooth table.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an occurrence, something that happens.

clue.text: 'e was up to wear down

parts.note: the dropped-aitch 'e is he, giving just E
a rider on horseback is up, so was up means rode

explanation.surface: A Cockney says he was ready to wear something down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was up' is jockey talk: a rider who is up is in the saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear away gradually, as water does to rock.

clue.text: See 20
Sounds like important team needed for loading area

indicators.note: says the phrase that follows is spoken, and its sound gives a differently written word

parts.note: key means important and a side is a team

explanation.surface: A star team are needed at the docks for loading.
explanation.definitionFit: A wharf edge is where ships are loaded and unloaded.

clue.text: Delegate deposited in river

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
put means deposited, laid down

explanation.surface: A delegate's body was deposited in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To depute is to delegate a task or authority to someone else.

clue.text: Narcotic proving gamble, with learner driver cutting strain when reversing

parts.note: bet means gamble

indicators.note: cutting says the learner piece slices into the strain piece
reversing means the word for strain is read backwards

parts.note: a strain is a tune
L is the learner plate driver

explanation.surface: A drug habit proves a gamble, while a learner driver cuts in while backing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when reversing' turns TUNE into ENUT, and L, a learner driver from the L-plate, goes in to give ELNUT.
explanation.definitionFit: The areca seed is chewed as a mild stimulant across South Asia, a narcotic in the broad sense.
